data.research_question: Normalize the Marcus Williamson violent-offenders packet into canonical StarIntel v0.9.0 machine-readable records while preserving allegation/adjudication boundaries and testing the sentencing-disparity claim.
data.method: Transform the existing sourced Markdown packet into typed person, source, evidence-record, legal-case, event, claim, analysis, and relation documents without adding victim identities.
classification_rules: Keep the nine Ohio robbery guilty pleas separate from the 2022 Tennessee allegation.
Do not represent the Tennessee conduct as a conviction.
Describe the Tennessee conduct as alleged violent kidnapping/aggravated robbery rather than as a mental-health episode.
Treat sentencing disparity as a descriptive analytic finding; do not infer causal favoritism without evidence.

findings.finding: Nine Ohio robbery guilty pleas are represented as adjudicated conduct.
The Tennessee violent kidnapping/aggravated-robbery conduct is represented as an allegation/charge with a separately reported non-prosecution disposition.
The reported no-immediate-prison outcome is represented as a reported disposition pending capture of the primary judgment.
The current comparator set supports a descriptive sentencing-disparity conclusion but not a causal favoritism conclusion.
